name: Anchor nav
purpose: In-page section navigation with scrollspy: links to headings inside the CURRENT document, where the link matching the section being read marks itself automatically as the reader scrolls. Two placements, one grammar — a sticky horizontal bar and a vertical 'on this page' rail. Use it on long single-page content (product terms, rates and fees, a long article) where the reader needs to see the shape of the page and jump inside it. Itinerary row 37 (P3, 'In-page section nav').
$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — new component, built through the gated-component route at #203 wave 3b lane I. Nothing about it is ruled.

props.name: placement
props.$note: Sticky horizontal bar above the content, or a vertical rail beside it. Structural variance — a different assembly, not a scaled parameter.

props.name: sections
props.$note: Ordered {id, label} pairs, one per section heading. The ids are real document ids — the links are real fragment links and work with JavaScript off.

props.name: currentId
props.$note: The section currently in view. Authored in the markup as the no-JS answer; the scrollspy only ever MOVES it.

props.name: offset
props.$note: Pixels of sticky chrome above the content. Drives both scroll-margin-top on the sections and the observer's top rootMargin — one number, two consumers.

variants.name: bar
variants.use: sticky horizontal strip at the top of the scrolling region; the current section carries a bottom bar

variants.name: rail
variants.use: vertical list beside the content; the current section carries a leading bar and a surface change

tokens.bar-bg: tertiary/background/default — the sticky bar and the rail surface, so they read as chrome over the prose
tokens.rule: divider/border/section — the outer frame and the bar's bottom edge
tokens.hover: tertiary/background/hover — hover AND the rail's current-row ground
tokens.indicator: primary/border/default (#DB0011, both modes) — the 3px current-section bar, matching the indicator navigations.meta.json describes for its (unbuilt) anchors variant
tokens.$note: Wrapping prose takes Editorial composites and single-line labels take Component ones — the type gate's own deciding rule. This snippet contributes 0 to the type-composite debt.

accessibility.landmarks: A <nav> landmark named 'On this page', so it is findable and skippable (2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).
accessibility.currentSection: aria-current="true", NOT "page" — the page has not changed, the reader's location within it has. Sidebar nav uses "page" for the inverse reason.
accessibility.sections: Each section is a <section> with aria-labelledby pointing at its own visible heading, so the region has a name.
accessibility.noJs: The initial current-section state is authored in the markup and every link is a real fragment link, so the component is correct and operable with JavaScript off. The IntersectionObserver is feature-detected and only ever moves the mark.
accessibility.targetArea: Every link is min-height 44px in both placements.
accessibility.colourIndependence: The current section is carried by aria-current + a bar whose presence/absence is a shape difference. Colour is third, never alone.
accessibility.motion: scroll-behavior:smooth is neutralised by the prefers-reduced-motion block, so an anchor jump lands instantly for a motion-sensitive reader.

antiPatterns: Building it as Tabs — tabs swap panels and remove the inactive ones from the document; an anchor nav hides nothing. Announcing one as the other is the classic defect this component exists to prevent
Marking the current section by the red bar alone
A scrollspy that only works with JavaScript — the authored state must stand on its own
Forgetting scroll-margin-top, so a jump lands with the heading hidden behind the sticky bar

behaviour.scrollspy: IntersectionObserver rooted on the scroll container, rootMargin '-56px 0px -55% 0px', threshold 0. The FIRST intersecting section in document order wins, so scrolling up and down produces a stable, monotonic mark rather than a flicker between two partly-visible sections.
behaviour.jump: Real fragment links plus scroll-margin-top on each section, so the heading clears the sticky bar.
behaviour.motion: standard ease only; smooth scrolling and every transition are neutralised under prefers-reduced-motion.
